name: Kings, Caravans and Freedom: Africa's Long Story
description: Africa told from the inside: Nile kingdoms, gold empires, trading cities, the slave trade, colonial carve-up and the struggles that brought independence.

checkpoints.name: The first kingdoms
checkpoints.note: Along the Nile the Kingdom of Kush rules, then the Kingdom of Aksum in the Ethiopian highlands trades with Rome and India. In West Africa the Ghana Empire grows rich on gold and salt. Ancient Egypt has its own book and is left out here.

checkpoints.name: Gold and learning
checkpoints.note: The Mali Empire's Mansa Musa shows his wealth on pilgrimage, Timbuktu becomes a centre of learning, and Great Zimbabwe and the churches of Lalibela rise in stone. Along the east coast Swahili trading towns link Africa to the Indian Ocean.

checkpoints.name: Kingdoms and the slave trade
checkpoints.note: Songhai, Kongo, Benin and Ashanti rule large states, and Benin's guilds of casters make the famous Benin Bronzes. Njinga resists Portuguese rule in Angola, but the Atlantic slave trade tears communities apart.

checkpoints.name: Carved up
checkpoints.note: Shaka builds the Zulu Kingdom and Livingstone crosses the continent. Europeans meet at the Berlin Conference and divide Africa in the Scramble, though Ethiopia wins at Adwa.

checkpoints.name: Awakening
checkpoints.note: Pan-Africanism spreads, Haile Selassie rules Ethiopia, and Kwame Nkrumah leads the Gold Coast toward independence as Ghana in 1957, as Kenyatta and the Mau Mau press the British in Kenya.

checkpoints.name: Independence and apartheid
checkpoints.note: A wave of new states appears, Lumumba leads the Congo, the OAU is founded and Achebe writes of the new Africa. In South Africa, Sharpeville, Soweto and Biko mark the fight against apartheid, which ends with Mandela and the 1994 election. In 1994 Rwanda suffers genocide.
